title: L.A.'s New Mayor Stands by Promise: No International Trips Before Taking Office
text:
Los Angeles Mayor Karen Bass has recently faced‍ significant backlash due to her response to the wildfires ​that swept through the‌ city.The criticism stems from two main issues: her decision to travel internationally during a critical time ‍and her previous budget cuts to the Fire Department.
Mayor Bass was out of the country when the wildfires began, specifically on a⁣ trip to Ghana.‌ This decision has been heavily criticized, as ⁢it coincided with the National Weather Service issuing warnings of “extreme ​fire weather conditions” [3[3 ]. Critics argue ⁣that her absence during this critical period was inappropriate and possibly harmful to the city’s response efforts.
Additionally, Mayor Bass had previously cut the Fire Department’s budget, which has also come under scrutiny in the wake of the wildfires.This budget cut has been ⁤seen as a ⁣contributing factor to the city’s ​inadequate response to the fires, further fueling the backlash against her [1[1 ].
Mayor Bass had previously ‌vowed⁣ not to travel internationally⁣ if elected, but this promise was not kept. As taking office, she has made multiple international trips, including three ⁤visits to France ‌for the 2024 Olympic Games in Paris [2[2 ].Her decision to travel internationally during the wildfires has⁣ been seen as a breach of this promise and has ⁢further angered the public.
The backlash has been severe, with rivals lashing out, liberal supporters whose homes burned down becoming outraged critics, and an online petition demanding her immediate resignation attracting over 100,000 signatures [3[3 ]. The political future⁣ of ‍Mayor‍ Bass ‌is now in doubt ‍due to these ⁣developments.it seems like your sharing a news article about Mayor Karen Bass of ⁣Los Angeles and her response to recent wildfires in the city. Here’s a summary and ‍some key points:
Mayor Bass’s Travel : Mayor bass recently traveled internationally, which was criticized ⁣given the ongoing wildfires in Los Angeles. her spokesman, Zach Seidl, defended the trip, stating it was at the request of the Biden‍ administration and ⁢that she ​was in constant contact with⁢ officials during the‍ fires. Response to Criticism : Mayor Bass acknowledged the city’s ⁢grief and anger,and has promised a full accounting of the response⁤ efforts once the fires are extinguished. She also urged​ residents ‍to unite and reject division. Return and Actions : Upon her return, Mayor Bass stated she took a military flight back to Los Angeles as ⁢quickly as possible and was in constant contact with officials during the fires. She visited the fire‍ zone in Pacific Palisades‌ instantly after landing. Collaborative Style : Mayor⁣ bass is known for her collaborative style and deep roots in Los Angeles. Here’s a brief extract from the article:
“At news conferences,⁢ Ms. Bass, 71, has repeatedly acknowledged the city’s grief ‍and anger, and​ urged residents to ‘lock arms’ and⁢ ‘reject those who seek to divide ​us.’ She has promised that after⁤ the fires are‍ extinguished,’we will ​have a full accounting of what worked and,especially,what⁤ did not.'”
“On Wednesday, soon ‌after her return, she ​said she ‍had made the trip ⁣at the request of the Biden administration, that she‍ had been in ‘constant contact’ with local, federal and ‍county officials after the fires broke out, and that she took‌ a military flight to get back as quickly as possible.”
Los Angeles Mayor’s Travels and civic Emergencies Los Angeles Mayor Karen Bass has earned a deep well of trust among the city’s mostly liberal voters.Her ⁣handling of crises before the ⁣wildfires had largely been applauded, including a series of mudslides and winter floods last ⁢year and the swift restoration of a section of Interstate 10 in 2023 after it was severely‍ damaged‌ by fire. ⁢Her⁤ acceptance ⁤of the Olympic ⁣flag during one of the trips to France, as⁣ the first black woman to represent a host city, was widely regarded as history-making, and her domestic travel frequently enough produced results that benefited her city.
In late April,she led a bipartisan delegation of mayors to Washington,D.C. There, she successfully lobbied federal leaders to expand veterans’ eligibility for housing vouchers, a change that⁣ is expected to be instrumental in‌ addressing homelessness in Los Angeles and across the U.S.However, her travel—both domestically and internationally—has at times complicated her handling of civic emergencies. Her trip to Ghana was not ‍the first time she was out of town when crises and news ⁣events big and small ‍broke ‍out.
During that late April trip to Washington, pro-Palestinian protests at U.C.L.A. turned violent.She cut the trip⁣ short and flew back on May 1, ⁢issuing statements along the way to reassure residents.
While she was in France for the closing ceremony of the olympics in August, Gov. Gavin Newsom showed up at a mid-city⁣ underpass to make the point that local governments ‍needed to do more to⁣ clear homeless encampments.While she was‍ in paris for the Paralympic ​Games in september, the National weather Service issued an excessive heat warning for los Angeles, with ⁤117-degree forecasts. Power outages forced the cancellation of a show at the Hollywood Bowl.
None‌ of those⁣ trips generated complaints. ​The U.C.L.A. protests were handled by a number of jurisdictions, and Los Angeles is scheduled to host the 2028 Olympic Games.
Municipal governance, like many other⁢ lines of work, has become increasingly mobile. Computers, cellphones, and video conferencing let elected leaders ⁢operate remotely, and chains of command specify who is in charge⁣ when⁣ an official is out of town or out of the office.
